newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, buoyed by U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, buoyed by U.S. markets.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to higher Friday, as the market tended higher in calm trade on the back of firm U.S. Treasuries.
"The market was firm above all because of the decline in the long U.S. bond yield," said a trader at a local bank. The U.S. 30-year yield was last at 6.66 percent, down one basis point.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 94-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.49 at 121.25.
Another trader said the market looked set to show more strength next week, considering the firmness of U.S. Treasuries and the decreasing likelihood of a U.S. rate hike next month.
"The scenario for the Latin American markets remains good for next week," said another trader. "The Argentine market continues to be underpinned."
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.60 percent from 5.55 percent.
